items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1970-02-14
items.q: Louis and I, we were back at the homes a while, see we spent all the time in the homes out there enjoying life

ctx.x: Yeah, well, Louis, well Louis, he's around my age too. Well, Louis and I, we were back at the homes a while, see we spent all the time in the homes out there enjoying life, you know. And, well he's been back there a good while, him, but I stayed a year back there. But, uh, after I got back there, I mean, the trees were so nice back there, but I used to come home every Saturday at 12 o'clock and go back, go back there Monday morning, you know what I mean? Seven o'clock, I had to be back there at 7 on a Monday. And…
I guess you never heard Bowden? No, no. Did you hear of him, or did you hear of him recently? No.

items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: And Louis Armstrong does that too.

ctx.x: time. I want to ask some more about Buddy Petit. I hope I don't make a news of his own. Oh no, no, no, no. But I never got to hear him. What kind of a tone did he have or what kind of a style? Did he play high notes, low notes most of the time? No, Buddy never did play no high notes.

Buddy was no high notes player. But what Buddy would put down there and in the staff, you're going to enjoy. Did he play a lot of notes? Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. Buddy had a whole lot of stuff, a whole lot of stuff but low. I mean he can go low and play more than when he can't high notes. He couldn't play no high notes and he's neck, you know what I mean? He used to come out right there. And Louis Armstrong does that too. Several people do. Yeah. And well I mean Louis come out on one side but Buddy's used to come out…
How was his teeth? In good shape? Yeah, he had nice teeth. Yeah. And Buddy was a nice looking boy. He was nice looking.
